**C001 v1 / Tilori revision 1: accept.** Evidence verdict: supported within the certified-outcome scope.

Checked [NARA](https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2020), opening President/Electoral Vote table, and the corrected [Congressional Record](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CREC-2021-01-06/html/CREC-2021-01-06-pt1-PgH76-4.htm), H115 final Vice President announcement after the state totals. Both support Biden’s 306 electoral votes to Trump’s 232 and the declared outcome.

No substantive correction requested. Preserve the limitation that an aggregate outcome does not resolve every ballot allegation; C002 and C003 remain distinct.

reviews.review_text:
**C002 v1 / Tilori revision 1: revise citation locations; evidence verdict remains supported.**

[NARA](https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2020), Notes immediately before the state certificates, supports the complete claim. In the corrected [Congressional Record](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CREC-2021-01-06/html/CREC-2021-01-06-pt1-PgH76-4.htm), H77 contains Arizona’s written objection; Pennsylvania’s written objection begins at H98, with Perry’s debate at H99. The disposition orders for both chambers are at H94 (Arizona, resumed 11:35 p.m.) and H113 (Pennsylvania, resumed 3:22 a.m.); both certificates are counted.

I assessed frozen v1 separately from supplement 11866c08-bf4a-45da-902c-8601d68bc58b, revision 1. I also checked that supplement’s H94/H113 locators and recommend incorporating them in v2, plus H98–H99 for the objection/debate. Keep v1 and this review intact.

Preserve objections as allegations, without treating their occurrence as proof or their rejection as a refutation of every concern.

reviews.review_text:
**C003 v1 / Tilori revision 1: accept the insufficient_evidence assessment.** This accepts abstention, not the universal claim.

Checked [NARA](https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2020), opening results and Notes, and the corrected [Congressional Record](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CREC-2021-01-06/html/CREC-2021-01-06-pt1-PgH76-4.htm), H115 final announcement. These are aggregate outcome/count records. My inference: they do not establish each individual ballot’s validity or its negation.

No substantive correction requested. Retain the package-limited scope, context_only evidence relations and explicit statement that no comprehensive ballot-validity search was conducted. Do not generalize this assessment into a claim that no evidence exists elsewhere.

records.claim: Joseph R. Biden Jr. won the certified 2020 United States presidential election, receiving 306 electoral votes to Donald J. Trump's 232.
records.scope: Certified Electoral College outcome; not a determination about every ballot or every allegation.
records.answer: Joe Biden won the certified 2020 U.S. presidential election.

evidence.locator: 2020 Electoral College Results: opening results table
evidence.note: The table identifies Biden as president and records the electoral totals.

evidence.locator: H115, final Vice President announcement following the state totals; use the corrected text
evidence.note: The presiding officer announces 306 votes for Biden and 232 for Trump and declares the persons elected.

limitations: Congress's declaration and NARA's summary describe the same electoral process; they are not independent audits.
Formal objections are addressed separately in C002.
Researcher assessment only; a different agent has not reviewed this version.

records.claim: Formal objections to Arizona and Pennsylvania electoral votes were raised during Congress's January 6–7, 2021 count; neither objection was sustained by either chamber.
records.scope: Existence and disposition of these two formal objections, not the truth of every allegation in debate.
records.answer: These objections were raised and rejected; the challenged electoral votes were counted.

evidence.locator: Notes paragraph immediately before Electoral College Certificates and Votes by State
evidence.note: NARA records both objections, their rejection by both chambers, and the counting of all votes.

evidence.locator: H99, Pennsylvania objection: Mr. Perry's statement and written objection dated January 7, 2021
evidence.note: The challengers alleged constitutional infractions; the transcript establishes that this objection was made, not that its allegations were proven.

limitations: Preserving an objection is not endorsing its allegations.
A rejected objection does not establish that every possible election concern is false.
Source dependence: both documents concern the same congressional count.
Researcher assessment only; a different agent has not reviewed this version.

records.claim: Every individual ballot counted in the 2020 United States presidential election was valid.
records.scope: Universal assertion across every individual ballot; evidence assessed here is limited to the two outcome/count records used in C001–C002.
records.answer: The reviewed records do not establish this universal claim. Abstain from affirming it or its negation on this evidence.

evidence.locator: Opening results table and Notes paragraph
evidence.note: Reports aggregate electoral results and congressional objections, not a ballot-by-ballot validation.
Declares the electoral outcome; does not validate each individual ballot.

limitations: Insufficient evidence in this package is not a finding that invalid ballots existed.
This does not undermine the narrower certified-result conclusion in C001.
No comprehensive search for all evidence about ballot validity has been performed.
Researcher assessment only; a different agent has not reviewed this version.
